correctness.rationale: The cone identity and derivative formulas follow from the actual 2x2 matrices in arXiv:2611.18062v1 Eq. (5). Each matrix is nonnegative and uniformly strictly substochastic. A cone-preserving induction gives strict order for every n,k. Uniform norm estimates and a telescoping product show TV <= C/[n(1-p*)²], while the exact k=1 tail supplies the sharp positive 1/n lower bound for nonzero Delta. Neutral feedback gives exact geometric distribution. A reproducible exact-rational and symbolic checker reconstructs core identities without reliance on experiments as proof.

originality.rationale: Jia, arXiv:2611.18062v1, Eq. (5), gives the underlying conditional matrix-product burst law and remarks on approximate geometric behavior. The assessed proposition is instead a strict sign-uniform stochastic ordering across every initial protein count and every tail, plus a uniform explicit total-variation upper bound and matching inverse-count lower bound. In the main paper’s inspected mathematical text, no order or quantitative convergence theorem covers these assertions. Bokes–Singh (2017) and Bokes (2022) study continuous-concentration drift-jump feedback and steady-state noise/distributions, not the exact discrete two-state RNA-binding conditional law. Literature searches and mathematical-record searches retrieved no implication of the specified two-component cone argument or its rate. Priority remains literature-bounded; the 2022 full text is unavailable.

value.rationale: The originating model highlights how RNA binding modulates burst noise but its conditional burst law is difficult to interpret and qualitatively only approximates a geometric law for large initial protein count. The new global stochastic order establishes all increasing-burst risk statistics move in the same direction with initial protein population, with no sign changes by burst threshold, and the optimal quantitative 1/n approximation rate locates when a geometric surrogate becomes reliable. These are interpretable all-parameter properties of a molecular feedback law, not a numerical example or a mere parameter restatement.
